title: Yehuda ben Peturi (Tanna)
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Bava Metzia 62a: 'Two people were walking on the road, and one of them had a jug of water. Ben Peturi expounded: It is better that both drink and die, and let not one of them see the death of his fellow — until R' Akiva came and taught: Your life takes precedence,' etc. (In the Tosefta, Zuckermandel edition, it reads 'R' Yehuda ben Peturi in the name of R' Akiva,' which Hyman calls an error.) And there, at the beginning of chapter 6: 'R' Yehuda says' (in the Tosefta, Zuckermandel edition: 'R' Yehoshua') 'in the name of Ben Peturi,' etc.; Hyman concludes: from this we see that he lived in the generation before them.

notes.text: “There, at the beginning of chapter 6” most likely refers back to the Tosefta, but Hyman does not name the work again.

Hyman reports two Zuckermandel Tosefta readings: Yehuda ben Peturi speaking in the name of Rabbi Akiva, which he calls an error, and Yehoshua in place of Yehuda in the second passage. His inference about Ben Peturi’s earlier generation is retained as his argument.

The Zuckermandel Tosefta, Sotah, printed p. 303, gives two distinct reports. Just before chapter 6, R. Yehoshua reports that R. Yehuda ben Peturi expounded the city boundaries in the name of R. Akiva. Chapter 6 opens with R. Yehoshua speaking in the name of ben Peturi about Job. The consulted Machon Mamre text gives R. Yehuda in the latter passage. The jug of water discussion is in Bava Metzia 62a, where the consulted text has ben Petora. Hyman calls the first Zuckermandel attribution an error and draws his inference about the earlier generation from the second.
